q1.saying: Most commenters call the two-axis framework a workable starting point but not a complete risk determination, asking FDA to account for reversibility, error detectability, time to harm, traceability, autonomy or clinical agency, and patient vulnerability. Many add that human oversight and downstream safeguards should lower risk only with proof they work; several say "incorrect output" omits harms of omission.

q13.saying: Commenters accept synthetic data only as a supplement — for rare events, adversarial and stress testing, controlled perturbations, and privacy-limited coverage — and not for establishing performance rates, subgroup claims, or benefit-risk conclusions. Most ask FDA to guard against correlated blind spots through generator lineage disclosure and separation, independent or multiple generators, real-world holdouts, and separate real/synthetic reporting.
